subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - fallout/secondary losses definition and parity
content:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-corp.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: MSA + Order Form - fallout/secondary losses wording

David,

Thanks for the updated MSA and Order Form. Legal reviewed the limitation of liability section and wants to push back on the one-way carve-out for consequential damages. Their view is that 'consequential' is too vague and could be used to bypass the cap on recoverable damages for loss that is fairly foreseeable from a service disruption. They suggested the term 'fallout losses' to capture downstream third-party impacts and asked us for a clearer exclusion list and examples.

Can your team propose language that narrows the carve-out or makes it mutual? We also flagged that Acme will insist on an explicit exceptions list (eg: bodily injury, IP indemnity, data breach notification costs).

Attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf (order form), redlines_fallout_clause.docx (their markup).

Best,
Samantha

---

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:46:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: MSA + Order Form - fallout/secondary losses wording

Forwarding Acme's ask — they want a clearer definition and want parity (mutual carve-out) or a much narrower one-way carve-out. Please see Samantha's notes and the attachments.

Quick thoughts: we need to avoid opening the floodgates. Our standard is one-way exclusion for consequential/incidental/punitive losses (Customer can't claim those), with narrow exceptions (breach of confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence). Acme's legal wants either: (A) mutual exclusion with a higher cap, or (B) an exceptions list that is broader than we like.

Can you draft two options to present:
- Option A: mutual exclusion but explicit carve-ins (data breach remediation, IP indemnity, personal injury) and keep cap at $5M or higher depending on their ARR.
- Option B: keep one-way exclusion but tighten the definition of 'fallout/secondary losses' with examples and limit temporal scope (only losses caused by third-party dependent systems as proximate result).

Laura/Karthik — can you coordinate with legal on language and include a short justification we can send to procurement?

Thanks,
David

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA + Order Form - fallout/secondary losses wording

David, Karthik — taking this. I'll draft both options and hand off to Legal for a quick sanity check. Notes from initial pass:

1) Terminology: I recommend we avoid introducing new jargon such as 'fallout losses' where possible. Instead, define 'consequential damages (also referred to as "fallout or secondary losses")' and then limit by concrete categories and examples. Keeps record consistent across deals.

2) Proposed tightening for one-way exclusion (Option B):
- Replace broad phrase with: "Consequential damages means any indirect, special, incidental, exemplary or punitive damages, including, without limitation, lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and third-party claims for loss of data or interruption of business, except to the extent such damages arise from Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Sections X (Confidentiality) or Y (IP Indemnity)."
- Add a temporal causation sentence: "Consequential damages exclude downstream third-party claims unless such claims are the proximate and direct result of a breach by Redwood that occurred within sixty (60) days of the event alleged by Customer."

3) Proposed mutual carve-out (Option A) sample language:
- "Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, indirect, exemplary, or punitive damages, except for damages arising from: (a) bodily injury; (b) death; (c) the indemnified IP claims; (d) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; or (e) the unauthorised disclosure of Customer Data as defined in Section Z."
- If mutual, we should push cap to 2x the proposed cap or to a floor tied to monthly committed spend. Procurement may accept if we tie to ARR/commitment.

4) Attachment suggestion: add a short 'examples' table in the Order Form to illustrate what counts as consequential vs direct. Reduces future disputes.

I'll produce drafts today and route to Legal (Karthik to introduce).

Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 13:21:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA + Order Form - fallout/secondary losses wording

Quick legal review notes — I did a rapid pass and agree with Laura's structure. A few redline suggestions:

- Remove ambiguous catch-all qualifiers like "without limitation" where they expand examples into lists; instead use "including, for example," which courts treat as illustrative.
- The "proximate and direct result" test is helpful but courts differ; adding a time-box (60 days) is a commercial compromise but not ironclad legally.
- For mutual carve-out option, propose a middle ground: mutual exclusion for consequential damages, but add an explicit carve-in for "reasonable third-party remediation costs" limited to verified invoices and pre-approved vendors. That helps Acme with downstream remediation concerns while protecting Redwood from speculative claims.
- Add obligation on Acme to mitigate and provide prompt notice within 30 days for any downstream third-party claim — failure to do so limits recoverable amounts.

I'll add redlines to the docx and return.

Karthik

I'll share a marked PDF of the cap proposal and their internal note on the remediation-costs mechanics tomorrow. Procurement expects the updated redline by Friday.
